opportunity.instructions: Judge ONLY the exact target expression under the supplied architecture profile. Supporting declarations and contracts explain this target; they are not additional candidates. Identify the subject, the alternatives distinguished by the predicate, and its demonstrated decision role. Use a supplied implementation for a helper call; judge a selected assembly as a whole without cherry-picking a lambda or guard. A pure declared predicate contract can establish a domain decision: executed side effects, multiple uses, high complexity and immediate code reduction are NOT required. Choose eligible when supplied evidence establishes a stable domain decision or domain behavior-selection contract whose definition benefits from a named, addressable, observable Specification. Choose excluded only with affirmative evidence of representation/parsing/I-O/adaptation mechanics without a distinct domain decision, or explicit evidence that a Specification already owns this SAME decision through its evaluation path. An unsafe error, a helper name, a permission-sounding field, branch count, imports, or a Specification elsewhere do not alone establish fit or same-decision ownership. A parser may enforce domain policy; a rejection or security-sounding check may also implement mechanics. For path checks, seek evidence of the contract for permitted domain references versus representation or generic adapter constraints; a declared integrity contract can suffice without actual filesystem access, but do not infer such a contract from the word unsafe. An isolated permission field can identify a topic without proving whether this site defines policy, adapts a verdict or merely reports it. Choose needs_review when a specific missing fact leaves materially different opportunity labels plausible. Do not require every caller or runtime binding when the supplied contract already settles this exact decision. Unknown ownership is not proof of ownership and does not automatically force abstention for an otherwise clear architectural-fit suggestion. Classify this axis independently: concern-kind uncertainty need not prevent eligible when both plausible responsibilities establish fit. Do not invent omitted facts or transfer labels from other evidence views.

criteria.eligible: Supplied evidence establishes a stable domain decision or domain behavior-selection contract suitable for a named, addressable, observable Specification; one use is sufficient. No supplied evidence establishes existing Specification ownership of this same decision.
criteria.excluded: Affirmative evidence establishes technical mechanics without a distinct domain decision, or explicit same-decision Specification ownership. Mere lack of policy evidence is not exclusion.
criteria.needs_review: A specific material ambiguity or missing fact prevents a reliable opportunity judgment. Abstention is unknown, not exclusion.

concern_kind.instructions: Independently classify the PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY of ONLY the exact target expression, using its supplied subject, alternatives and decision role. Supporting code establishes meanings and effects; do not classify an entire containing function or unrelated later decisions. A pure declared domain predicate can be policy without executing effects. Policy decides domain admissibility, authority, evidence sufficiency, eligibility, lifecycle obligations or which domain work has precedence. Mechanics parses, represents, transports, adapts or performs generic technical enforcement without a demonstrated distinct domain decision. A validation branch can enforce either role: rejection, an unsafe message, names and file location alone do not settle it. A supplied contract restricting permitted domain references can establish path-integrity policy even inside a parser and without actual filesystem access; generic path checks without a settled role must not automatically become either policy or mechanics. Variant_behavior selects a variant-specific implementation or behavior for an already established domain activity. Tie rule: a predicate deciding WHETHER work is allowed/required or WHICH obligation takes precedence is policy; selection of HOW an already established activity is implemented for a domain variant is variant_behavior. Testing an enum, boolean or none sentinel does not by itself establish variant_behavior. If the target only recognizes an external syntactic tag to construct typed facts, that dispatch is mechanics. Apply the tie rule to the selected expression: subsequent dispatch among individual handlers does not turn a preceding lifecycle-priority predicate into variant_behavior. If independently meaningful policy and adaptation are mixed in the selected expression and its primary contract cannot be established, choose unknown rather than silently changing target boundaries. Identifiers are evidence of a possible subject, not proof of enforcement or of the primary role; do not infer an operative permission gate from a permission-sounding field alone. A responsibility can be clear while Specification suitability or ownership remains unknown. Existing Specification ownership does not turn policy into mechanics. Choose unknown only for material ambiguity; ordinary unshown consumers are not a reason to abstain when the supplied expression or declared contract already settles responsibility. Do not infer omitted dependencies or copy labels from another evidence view.

criteria.policy: A demonstrated durable domain admissibility, authority, trust, evidence, eligibility, lifecycle or obligation-priority decision; validation and pure predicates can implement it.
criteria.mechanics: A demonstrated parsing, representation, I/O, adaptation or generic technical-enforcement responsibility without a distinct domain decision.
criteria.variant_behavior: Selection of variant-specific domain implementation or behavior for an already established activity, rather than eligibility or obligation precedence.
criteria.unknown: The supplied evidence does not establish a reliable primary responsibility; do not guess from names or silently split a mixed target.

The deploy job now computes a checksum-aware payload stage for each independently
manifested surface:

- the root SpecGraph artifact bundle;
- Team Decision Log;
- Hosted Operation Canary.

The staging tool compares each local `artifact_manifest.json` with the manifest
at the durable HTTPS base and copies only added or content-changed payload files
into one remote-root-shaped staging directory. Manifest-matched files are also
checked at the HTTPS origin, so a missing or stale payload is staged again and
the next deploy self-heals partial publication. Removed files remain physically
present because the shared webroot is non-destructive, but the new manifest no
longer authorizes them.

Deployment uploads the changed payload first, then each `checksums.sha256`, and
finally each `artifact_manifest.json`. A post-upload verifier downloads each
published manifest, checksum file, and manifest-authorized payload from all
three HTTPS bases and checks its SHA-256. A missing, malformed, partial, or
digest-mismatched public surface fails the job.

The changed payload mirror uses four parallel transfers. This is a bounded
transport optimization for high-latency SFTP hosts; checksums and manifests
remain sequential finalization writes after every payload transfer completes.

The Hosted Operation Canary bundle also publishes its scoped initialization
execution report at the top-level `runs/` bootstrap path. That single
public-safe alias lets SpecSpace discover and validate the durable workspace
binding before it follows the binding's scoped `runs/hosted-operation-canary`
refs. The remaining artifacts stay scoped and are not flattened by route slug.

## Authority Boundary

This proposal changes static artifact transport only. It does not:

- delete remote webroot files;
- publish files absent from a public-safe manifest;
- start Platform or hosted workers;
- execute managed operations;
- mutate canonical specs or Ontology packages;
- approve candidates, create Git reviews, or publish read models.

Remote manifests are planning hints, not final authority. Successful
post-publication HTTP digest verification is required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unchanged files are absent from the staged payload.
- Changed root and workspace payloads retain their relative durable URL paths.
- Path traversal and local digest mismatches fail closed.
- Payload upload precedes checksums and manifest finalization.
- Payload transfer parallelism is explicitly bounded.
- All three published surfaces receive post-upload HTTP digest verification.
- Hosted Operation Canary exposes a public-safe initialization bootstrap alias
  without flattening the remaining scoped run artifacts.
- Root-level `mirror --delete` remains forbidden.
- Static bundle safety validation and existing publication tests pass.

Deployment mirrors the contents of `dist/specgraph-public/` into
`SFTP_REMOTE_ROOT`. It must not create a nested `specgraph-public/` directory on
the static host.

Artifact deployment is intentionally non-destructive for the webroot. The
workflow must not run a root-level `mirror --delete` because the same
`SFTP_REMOTE_ROOT` can also contain the public landing page and hosting-managed
files. Consumers should use `artifact_manifest.json` and `checksums.sha256` as
the authoritative artifact index instead of inferring validity from every file
that happens to remain under `specs/` or `runs/`.

Proposal `0215` makes the payload transfer checksum-aware. The deploy job
compares each local manifest with its durable HTTPS manifest and stages only
added or content-changed files for the root, Team Decision Log, and Hosted
Operation Canary surfaces. Manifest-matched payload bytes are checked at the
HTTPS origin so a rerun stages and repairs missing or stale files after partial
publication. It uploads payload files first, then checksums, and manifests last.
A post-upload pass verifies the published manifest, checksum file, and every
manifest-authorized payload, so an incomplete or stale public surface fails
closed.
Remote files omitted by a new manifest are not deleted from the shared webroot;
they simply stop being authoritative.

def candidate_move(
    node: workspace.SpecNode,
    *,
    source_path: str,
    gate_order: list[str],
    status_order: list[str],
) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    if node.status not in VALID_STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported canonical status for {node.id}: {node.status}")
    gate = node.gate_state
    if gate != "none":
        if gate not in gate_order or gate not in GATE_ACTIONS:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported gate state for {node.id}: {gate}")
        kind, next_gap, hint_template = GATE_ACTIONS[gate]
        command_hint = hint_template.format(spec_id=node.id)
        rank = gate_order.index(gate)
    elif node.status in status_order:
        next_gap = "targeted_refinement"
        command_hint = f"Run a targeted dry-run for {node.id}, then refine one bounded concern."
        rank = len(gate_order) + status_order.index(node.status)
        kind = "refine_spec"
    else:
        return None

    return rank, {
        "kind": kind,
        "spec_id": node.id,
        "title": node.title,
        "status": node.status,
        "gate_state": gate,
        "next_gap": next_gap,
        "source_artifact": source_path,
        "command_hint": command_hint,
        "review_required": True,
    }

def _evaluate(self, candidate: BDDContext, recorder: TraceRecorder | None) -> bool:
        return not self.findings(candidate)

POLICIES = (
    BDDProfileSelectionSpec(),
    BDDContainerPresenceSpec(),
    BDDScenarioFieldsSpec(),
    BDDScenarioValuesSpec(),
    BDDScenarioIDsSpec(),
    BDDScenarioReferencesSpec(),
)

for policy in POLICIES:
        skip = policy.skip_reason(context)
        if skip:
            if recorder is not None:
                recorder.skipped(policy.rule_ref)
            outcomes.append(PolicyOutcome(policy.rule_ref, "skipped", skip))
            continue
        passed = policy.is_satisfied_by(context, recorder=recorder)
        current_findings = policy.findings(context)
        findings.extend(current_findings)
        outcomes.append(PolicyOutcome(policy.rule_ref, "satisfied" if passed else "unsatisfied"))
        context = policy.transition(context, current_findings)

def dump_canonical_yaml(data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    rendered = yaml.safe_dump(
        data,
        sort_keys=False,
        allow_unicode=True,
        default_flow_style=False,
        width=100,
    )
    if not rendered.endswith("\n"):
        rendered += "\n"
    return rendered

def format_file(path: Path) -> bool:
    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    canonical = canonicalize_text(source)
    if source == canonical:
        return False
    path.write_text(canonical, encoding="utf-8")
    return True
